questions.question: A 35-year-old patient presents with itchy plaques over elbows and knees. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales over extensor surfaces (elbows and knees) is the classic presentation of plaque psoriasis (Psoriasis vulgaris).

questions.question: A 50-year-old man presents with acute abdomen and guarding. The X-ray finding suggests:
questions.explanation: Free air under the right dome of the diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum) on an erect chest radiograph confirms a perforated hollow viscus requiring urgent surgical exploration.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered the drug of choice for anaphylactic shock in adults?
questions.explanation: Intramuscular Epinephrine (1:1000 dilution, 0.5 mg) in the anterolateral thigh is the first-line life-saving intervention for anaphylaxis.

questions.question: The definitive diagnostic test for Hirschsprung's disease is:
questions.explanation: Rectal suction biopsy showing an absence of ganglion cells in the submucosal (Meissner) and myenteric (Auerbach) plexuses with elevated acetylcholinesterase staining is the gold standard.

questions.question: Which cranial nerve is tested by assessing sensation over the anterior two-thirds of the tongue?
questions.explanation: General somatic sensation from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue is carried by the lingual nerve (branch of CN V3). Taste sensation from the same region is mediated by the chorda tympani (CN VII).
